jitter — 3D augment op

• Data kinds: points → points

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.jitter(points, sigma: 'float', clip: 'Optional[float]' = None, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import pcl_augment; pcl_augment.jitter(points, sigma: 'float', clip: 'Optional[float]' = None, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, ops3d.get("jitter"))

Usage

Add isotropic Gaussian noise N(0, sigma) to each point (mimicking sensor position noise).

sigma is the standard deviation in world units (user-specified parameter). If clip is given, each component of the displacement is truncated to [-clip, clip] (suppressing outlying displacements). For large N the noise has mean≈0 and standard deviation≈sigma. The return value has the same shape as the input, (N,3).

• sigma < 0 raises ValueError. sigma == 0 or empty input returns a copy of the input.

• clip, if given, must be > 0 (anything else raises ValueError). Truncation is per component, so

the length of a displacement vector is at most √3·clip.

• Deterministic with seed (np.random.default_rng(seed)). Same seed and same shape give the same noise.

• Input must be (N,3) finite values only (a 1-D array of length 3 is promoted to 1 point; anything else, or NaN, raises

ValueError). The return value is float64.

• When measuring the noise robustness of registration (register_fpfh etc.), choosing sigma as a ratio to the point spacing

(e.g. the grid width of voxel_grid_downsample) makes conditions easier to compare.
